records.title: Electrical warning signs
records.content: A burning smell, smoke, sparks, exposed wiring, or water near electrical equipment may indicate a safety hazard. Recommend urgent human assessment.

records.title: Active water leaks
records.content: Water dripping from a ceiling or a leaking pipe is generally a plumbing issue. Active leaks that may damage equipment need prompt attention. Water near electrical equipment requires urgent safety review.

records.title: Air conditioner not cooling
records.content: An air conditioner that runs but does not cool is normally an air-conditioning issue. Without additional safety warning signs, moderate urgency is appropriate.

records.title: Minor routine repairs
records.content: A loose door handle or similar minor fixture problem with no immediate safety risk is generally routine maintenance.

records.title: Flickering lights
records.content: A flickering light is normally an electrical issue. Flickering alone may be moderate urgency. Flickering combined with a burning smell, smoke, sparks, or exposed wiring is a potential critical electrical hazard.

records.title: Incomplete or ambiguous reports
records.content: When a report lacks enough information to identify the problem, do not invent missing facts. Use an unknown or uncertain outcome where supported and flag the case for human review.

records.title: Water near electrical equipment
records.content: When water is near an electrical outlet, power strip, or other electrical equipment, treat the situation as a potential safety hazard even if the source of the water is uncertain. Recommend urgent human assessment.
